text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National commission in charge of election follow-up to devote 90 million dirhams ($9.6 million) to support political parties' campaigns.
- Cabinet meeting considers draft laws on collection of public receivables.
- France says it backs four-month mandate extension of U.N. Mission for Referendum in Western Sahara.
- Morocco lifts controls on banana imports.
- Fisheries, Merchant Navy Minister Sahel tells Paris-based magazine Jeune Afrique he wants more active measures against illegal fishing with help of European Union.
- Interior Ministry says in report Morocco arrested more than 18,000 people for drug trafficking in 1996 including 315 foreigners.
- Tourism Minister M'daghri forecasts four million tourists in 2001, up from 1.7 million in 1997.
